uncited: 2D Refinement Layers is an optional post-processing module applied to rendered images to enhance texture detail and prevent "texture sticking" artifacts under viewpoint changes.

It builds on [CNN Post-Processing Network](7179-cnn-post-processing-network.md) by specifically employing alias-free convolutional layers to ensure temporal and spatial consistency when the camera moves.
It addresses the limitation of standard CNNs where high-frequency details may appear to stick to the image plane rather than the 3D geometry.
The refinement network is a shallow 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN).
- Layer Dimension: 16 channels per layer.
**Input Preparation**: Take the rendered image $I_{rendered}$.
**First Convolutional Layer**: Apply a $3 \times 3$ convolution with 16 output channels to the input.
The convolution uses alias-free layers with critical sampling.
**Second Convolutional Layer**: Apply a $3 \times 3$ convolution with 16 output channels to the result of step 3.
This layer also uses alias-free layers with critical sampling.
- **Texture Sticking**: Standard CNNs may cause textures to stick to the 2D image plane during viewpoint changes.
Using alias-free layers with critical sampling mitigates this.
- **Optional Application**: The refinement is optional and depends on the dataset.
It may not be necessary for all scenes or datasets.
- **Time Complexity**: Not given in the sources.
However, as a shallow CNN with small kernel sizes and low channel dimensions, it is computationally lightweight compared to the volume rendering process itself.
- **Memory Complexity**: Not given in the sources.
The network has a small number of parameters ($16 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3 + 16 \times 16 \times 3 \times 3 + 16 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3$ weights, plus biases), fitting easily in memory.
- **When to use**: When rendering images that exhibit texture sticking artifacts or when higher texture fidelity is required.
- **When not to use**: When computational resources are extremely limited and the visual improvement is negligible, or for datasets where the base rendering is already sufficient.
It leverages alias-free layers [21] to ensure that the refinement does not introduce artifacts that are inconsistent with 3D geometry.
The approach is part of a broader effort to improve the visual quality of neural volume rendering methods.
